World’s Largest Hardware Wallet Maker Ledger Investigates Wallet-Draining Reports; Onchain Analyst Estimates Losses Above $86M Ledger, the world’s largest hardware wallet manufacturer, said it is investigating reports of stolen funds involving users in Southeast Asia who purchased devices from reseller CryptoBilis. The company has asked CryptoBilis to pause sales and shipments during the investigation and advised customers who bought devices from the reseller within the past 90 days not to initialize them. Users who have already set up their devices were advised to move assets to a new Ledger signer using a new seed phrase. Separately, onchain investigator Specter said he traced suspicious addresses receiving funds from hundreds of victim wallets across Ethereum, TRON and Bitcoin, estimating total losses at more than $86 million. The common attack vector has not yet been confirmed, and there is currently no evidence that Ledger hardware wallets or Ledger’s core infrastructure were directly compromised. CZ said that, based on information available so far, the Ledger wallet thefts appear to be localized to a supply-chain attack involving a single vendor, with a small number of users likely having purchased fake or tampered Ledger devices. He added that BNB ecosystem participants and the broader industry would help trace and recover the stolen funds. According to MistTrack, Tether is freezing USDT across multiple addresses linked to the Ledger user theft incident. MistTrack said the losses it is currently tracking are approaching $90 million, with several affected users having contacted its team for assistance. — link

U.S. Consumer Sentiment Weakens as Inflation Expectations Climb to Five-Month High The University of Michigan’s preliminary October consumer sentiment index fell to 46.3 from 48.1, below the 47.6 forecast. Current conditions dropped sharply to 44.7 from 50.9, while the expectations index edged up to 47.3 from 46.3. One-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7% and five-year expectations to 3.5%, both the highest since May, as high prices and borrowing costs continued to weigh on consumers. — link

Bessent Says U.S. May Seize About $1B in Iran-Linked Crypto This Week According to Newsmax, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said at the NPolicy Summit in Washington that the U.S. may seize about $1 billion in cryptocurrency linked to Iran this week, adding that authorities “know where it is.” He said the move is part of an “absolute isolation campaign” that also includes maritime blockades, flight restrictions and efforts to close Iran’s land routes. Bessent said in May that the U.S. had already seized about $1 billion in Iran-linked crypto assets, although it remains unclear whether the latest $1 billion target is additional to previously announced seizures. — link

Tether Temporarily Freezes 1.45 Million USDT in THORChain Vaults on TRON, Reverses Blacklisting After Three Hours The Defiant reported that Tether temporarily blacklisted four THORChain vault addresses on TRON, freezing approximately 1.45 million USDT and forcing THORChain to suspend TRON-related swaps and certain functions. THORChain co-founder Chad Barraford said the team had received no prior notice. About three hours later, all four addresses were removed from the blacklist, with their USDT balances remaining intact, and THORChain subsequently restored the affected services. Another 19 addresses blacklisted in the same batch remained on the blacklist at the time. Tether has not explained the reason for the freeze, and no connection to any specific crypto theft has been confirmed. — link
